clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old female presented in November 2020 with persistent left-sided pulsatile tinnitus lasting 10 months. Initial three-dimensional TOF MR angiography demonstrated a small hyperintense signal region at the lesser sphenoid wing and left para-cavernous sinus, extending to venous outlets including the superior ophthalmic vein, inferior ophthalmic vein, and meningeal emissary veins into the pterygoid plexus, consistent with a dural arteriovenous fistula (DAVF). The fistula vascular anatomy and drainage patterns align with Cognard IIa classification despite absence of explicit source diagnostic classification. Over 30 months from onset, clinical follow-up documented abrupt cessation of tinnitus, with the tinnitus handicap inventory score decreasing from 32 to 0. Follow-up 3D-TOF MR angiography at 30 months showed no residual hyperintense signals or abnormal flow, consistent with spontaneous fistula closure. The diagnosis is supported by temporal correlation of symptoms and imaging findings and resolution consistent with clinical course.

Follow-up MR angiography 30 months after onset showed no residual abnormal signals, indicating spontaneous closure of the fistula.
